{{nihongo|'''Ichisuka Shrine'''|一須何神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

'''Ichisuka Shrine''' (いちすかじんじゃ, 壹須何神社, 壱須何神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}{{ill|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|ar|محافظة ميناميكاواشي (أوساكا)|arz|محافظه ميناميكاواشى, اوساكا|ca|Districte de Minamikawachi|ceb|Minamikawachi-gun|de|Minamikawachi-gun|eo|Distrikto Minamikawachi|es|Distrito de Minamikawachi|fr|District de Minamikawachi|id|Distrik Minamikawachi, Ōsaka|it|Distretto di Minamikawachi|ja|南河内郡|ko|미나미카와치군|lt|Minamikavačio apskritis|pl|Powiat Minamikawachi|sr|Област Минамикавачи|uk|Повіт Мінамі-Кавачі|zh|南河內郡|qid=Q1347323}}{{ill|Kanan, Osaka|arz|بلده كانان, اليابان|ca|Kanan|ceb|Kanan Chō|eo|Kanan (Osaka)|es|Kanan (Osaka)|fa|کانان، اوساکا|fr|Kanan|hy|Կանան|it|Kanan|ja|河南町|ko|가난정|ms|Kanan, Osaka|my|ခနန်မြို့၊ အိုဆာကာ|pl|Kanan|ru|Канан|simple|Kanan, Osaka|sv|Kanan, Osaka|tl|Kanan, Osaka|tr|Kanan, Japonya|uk|Канан (Осака)|ur|کانان، اوساکا|zh|河南町|qid=Q2305508}} (formerly {{ill|Ishikawa|Q18700174|qid=Q18700174|lt=Ishikawa Village}}). It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former shrine rank was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

* {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}} (あまてらすおおかみ)

; Associated deities

* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Oshihomimi-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|de|Ninigi|eo|Ninigi|es|Ninigi no Mikoto|fa|نینیگی-نو-میکوتو|fr|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|id|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|it|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|ko|니니기|mni|ꯅꯤꯅꯤꯒꯤ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Ninigi|no|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|pl|Ninigi|pt|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ru|Ниниги но Микото|simple|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|sv|Ninigi|th|นินิงิ โนะ มิโกโตะ|tl|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|tr|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|uk|Нініґі но мікото|vi|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|zh|瓊瓊杵尊|qid=Q1056017|lt=Amatsuhikohikohoninigi-no-Mikoto}}

* {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188|lt=Kamuyamato Iwarebiko-no-Mikoto}} – the above five deities were formerly enshrined at Furubata Shrine

This area was the base of the {{ill|Soga clan|Q909854|qid=Q909854}} descendants, the {{ill|Ishikawa clan|Q615039|qid=Q615039|lt=Ishikawa no Ason}}, and sources such as *Kawachi no Kuni Shikijin Shikō* and *Watarai-shi Shinjin Nabari Kōshō* state that it was originally dedicated to the ancestral founder Soga no Ishikawa no Sukune. The current enshrined deities are thought to have been established in the early Edo period, and during the Edo period the shrine was called “Tenjin.” *{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Dai Nihon Jingi Shi}}* records it as “currently popularly known as Ichikawa Myōjin.”

=== History ===
Although the circumstances of its founding are unknown, the area was the base of the {{ill|Ishikawa clan|Q615039|qid=Q615039|lt=Ishikawa no Ason}}, and as it forms part of the {{ill|Ichisuka Kofun Cluster|Q11353283|qid=Q11353283}}, it is believed to have originally stood atop a burial mound. In the *{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}*, it is listed as a minor shrine.

During the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ar|فترة نانبوكو تشو|bg|Нанбоку-чо|bn|নান্‌বোকু-চোও যুগ|ca|Període Nanboku-chō|cs|Období Nanbokučó|de|Namboku-chō|es|Período Nanbokuchō|eu|Nanboku-chō Aroa|fa|دوره نانبوکوچو|fi|Nanboku-chō-kausi|fr|Époque Nanboku-chō|he|תקופת שתי החצרות הקיסריות|hu|A japán császári udvar különválása|id|Zaman Nanboku-chō|it|Periodo Nanboku-chō|ja|南北朝時代 (日本)|ko|남북조 시대 (일본)|ms|Tempoh Nanboku-chō|nl|Nanboku-cho-periode|pt|Período Nanboku-chō|ru|Период Намбокутё|simple|Nanboku-chō period|sr|Нанбокућо период|sv|Nanboku-chō|th|ยุคราชสำนักเหนือ-ใต้|tr|Nanboku-chō Dönemi|uk|Період Намбокутьо|vi|Nam–Bắc triều (Nhật Bản)|zh|南北朝时代 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Nanboku-tyô sî-tāi|zh_yue|南北朝 (日本)|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, the Southern Court’s {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ishikawa Castle}} was built here, and the shrine suffered repeated damage from warfare. In {{ill|1589|Q6759|qid=Q6759}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 17), {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550}} issued a certificate granting prayers and precinct privileges through the {{ill|Ishikawa district|ja|石川郡 (大阪府)|zh|石川郡 (大阪府)|qid=Q11586399|lt=Ishikawa District magistrate}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Itō Kaganokami Hidemori}}. A ceremonial hot-water cauldron dedicated at that time remains as a shrine treasure.<ref name="Kanan Town">[http://www.town.kanan.osaka.jp/kananchotte/kankogaido/terajinja/1494915847108.html　Ichisuka Shrine - Kanan Town] Accessed February 9, 2019</ref>

In the *{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawachi Meisho Zue}}*, published in 1801 ({{ill|Kyōwa|Q960763|qid=Q960763}} 1), it states: “Ichisuka Shrine is located in Ichisuka Village, referred to in the Engishiki as the present Tenjin. It is the tutelary shrine of this village and Ōgatsuka Village. An Eleven-faced Kannon is enshrined in the temple-shrine complex.” In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was ranked as a village shrine, and in 1907 (Meiji 40), it {{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700|lt=merged}} the village shrines Sugawara Shrine (Ōaza Higashiyama, Ishikawa Village) and Furubata Shrine (Ōaza Minami-Ōtomo, {{ill|Ōtomo|Q18700091|qid=Q18700091}}).

; Access
